To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mannosylerytrhitol lipid (MGL) stimulates the phosphorylation and activity of ERK, and that MGL induces characteristics of neuronal cell differentiation in rat pheochromcytoma PC12 cells through activation of ERK and c-Jun, via an overlapping signal cascade with that induced by NGF.
MEL induces the differentiation of PC12 cells through a signaling pathway that is partially overlapping to that activated by NGF, with activation of the transcription factor c-Jun as a key event.

MEL, a yeast extracellular mannosyleryhritol lipid, induces neuronal characteristics in PC12 cells by a signaling cascade that includes the transcription factors c-Fos and c-Jun, as well as the ERK protein kinase, and that the sequence elements required for MEL-induced activation of the c-june gene are located between -126 and -78 in the 5 flanking region of the gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new compounds that may serve as therapeutic agents for the treatment of human cancers.
the development of new drugs from microbial products.

the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying the differentiation of neuronal cells, and with the identification of extracellular glycolipoproteins that can be used as novel reagents to induce differentiation of neuronal cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the yeast extracellular glycosylated lipid MEL induces characteristics in the PC12 cells that resemble neuronal differentiation.
MEL induces the differentiation of PC12 cells through a signaling pathway that involves ERK and that the activation of the c-juns promoter is required for MEL-mediated differentiation.
the yeast glycolipid MEL induces characteristics associated with the neuronal differentiation of PC12 cells via an ERK-dependent signaling pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that a glycolipid from yeast can induce neuronal differentiation in rat pheochromacytoma cells through a signal cascade that is partly overlapping the one activated by nerve growth factor.
MEL, a glycolipid from yeast cell wall, induces characteristics of neuronal cell differentiation, such as neurite extension and acetylcholinestease activity, in rat pheochromacytoma cells.
we have shown for the first time that the extracellular glycolibids from yeast, mannosylerytritol lipid, induce neuronal differentiation in PC-12 cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microbial extracellular glycoproteins and glycolipids can be used as novel reagents in medicine.

microbial extracellular glycoconjugates, such as MEL, may have potential therapeutic value in the treatment of cancer, because they induce cell death in tumor cells and stimulate cell differentiation in normal cells.
MEL induces differentiation of PC12 cells via an ERK-dependent mechanism that is similar to the one used by NGF.
